paragraphs.text: Benito Sarabia Olguín participated in Shipment TAM-11-01 on 2011-12-05. Pacto del Faro Gris was linked to Shipment TAM-11-01 on 2011-12-05. Shipment TAM-11-01 occurred at Tampico on 2011-12-05. Regional press reporting from the Tampico waterfront described a load of 60 kg of cocaine that left the port by small boat toward Houston, carried in the vessel local reporters identified as Panga Manta Oscura. One column named Sarabia, the Tampico plaza boss for Pacto del Faro Gris known on the docks as El Sastre, as the organizer and described the load as paperwork-covered by a guesthouse firm, Posada Arroyo Pardo, whose name appeared on the boat's registration.

Ignacio Treviño Salcido led Pacto del Faro Gris from 2011-01-22 until 2016-03-09. The same column described Treviño as the head of the pact and stated that Sarabia ran the Tampico docks for him under the pact's original division of the three ports. The column added that the Tampico crew had been pressing for a larger share of the Gulf highway lanes and speculated that the boat run was intended to show the crew could move product without the highway.

This digest summarizes open press reporting and carries no classification beyond the public domain. The reporting office has not corroborated the press accounts through its own sources. The Tampico press in this period was closely read by the crews it described, and the reporting office cannot exclude that the column was planted to embarrass the Tampico crew. The quantity reported is the figure printed in the column and has not been verified. The nickname attributed to Sarabia is shared with a figure in another network and the attribution here is the columnist's.
